articles.title: While stock lasts, you can now just buy a 512GB Steam Machine
articles.summary: Valve have given a fresh update on the queue system for the Steam Machine, and while stock exists you can just buy the 512GB Steam Machine right now.

articles.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
articles.summary: Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

articles.title: Claude Code v2.1.329
articles.summary: Added a "Server message" row to a server's page in /mcp that shows the JSON-RPC error message of a remote HTTP MCP server that refuses the connection.

articles.title: MiSTer WiFi / CIFS / Network Loading Fix
articles.summary: If you’re someone who configured your MiSTer to load games from your network, this post is for you! My MiSTer recently stopped showing my network folder when loading games.

articles.title: Samsung’s mobile division has someone new in charge for the first time in years
articles.summary: After the better part of 7 years, Samsung’s mobile division has a new chief and it’s Choi Won-Joon, who is already off to a great start with the successful launch of Galaxy Z Fold 8.

articles.title: Steam Frame hits over 300 Standalone Verified games
articles.summary: The Steam Frame has been out for a little while, and the amount of games that are properly playable in standalone has hit over 300.

articles.title: Friday the 13th NES to SNES Conversion
articles.summary: Developer Dustin Dembrosky aka “Dasutin” has just released his first NES to SNES port, for the game Friday the 13th. The port includes all of the typical enhancements you’d get with NES to SNES ports, such as no sprite flicker or slow downs.

articles.title: DabbleCAD Takes Design Offline
articles.summary: These days, there are all kind of online-only and in-browser CAD packages. DabbleCAD is the opposite of all that— a simple, offline, open-source design solution.

articles.title: Google’s 3D emoji has wild Android spec requirements: 10GB of free space, 6GB RAM
articles.summary: Google announced 3D emoji in May , with the new design shipping on the Pixel 11 in August . It has since arrived on older Pixel devices .

articles.title: The Tower Must Fall - review, build up a ridiculous tower with incremental upgrades
articles.summary: The Tower Must Fall is a curious fusion of tower defense with incremental progression, where you'll watch your precious creation fall time and time again.

articles.title: Walter Isaacson on curiosity and creativity in the AI age.
articles.summary: On our newest episode of Dialogues on Technology and Society, Kent Walker sits down with biographer and historian Walter Isaacson to talk about why history's biggest breakthroughs have always been a team sport.

articles.title: Preventing a Garage Door Opener From Rebooting When Offline
articles.summary: It’s always great when a smart garage door opener allows for easy local integration into a smart home network, but it’s not so nice when said device still insists on connecting to certain remote servers, and even reboots constantly due to time-outs.

articles.title: System76 released the Thelio Prime, a small and powerful Linux PC for work and play
articles.summary: The redesigned Thelio Prime has an internal volume of just 9.78 liters, 48.5% smaller than the original, while retaining desktop-class performance for everything you do, from everyday work to PC gaming.

articles.title: Google's latest AI model is faster, cheaper and smarter than its flagship predecessor from just weeks ago
articles.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in seven weeks, which is nearly 2x faster than its sibling Carbon, outperforms it on most benchmarks and comes in at a significantly lower price.

articles.title: Second iOS 27.3 and macOS Golden Gate 27.3 Public Betas Now Available
articles.summary: Apple today seeded the second betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.3, tvOS 27.3, and watchOS 27.3. Apple also has revised betas of of iOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3 available for developers.

articles.title: Expanding Android developer verification in 2027
articles.summary: We announced Android developer verification in 2025 as an extra layer of security that helps deter bad actors and makes it harder for them to repeatedly spread harm.

articles.title: HomeView woes, iPhone Duo face unlock, macOS Full Disk Access changes
articles.summary: Benjamin and Chance discuss their HomeView experiences and Siri reliability issues after a week of the product being in the world. Benjamin also tests the new Apple TV surround sound feature.

articles.title: Improvements on the pull request overview in public preview
articles.summary: This preview is very much a starting point, not the finished pull request experience. Try it on your next pull request. What is easier to find?

articles.title: App Store Award finalists announced
articles.summary: Every year, the App Store Awards celebrate the very best and most impactful apps and games on the App Store, and the developers behind them.

articles.title: Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps generally available
articles.summary: Enterprise Live Migrations (ELM) from Azure DevOps Services to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency is now generally available. You can move your repositories while your teams keep working, then cut over on your schedule.

articles.title: Red Hat Enterprise Linux runner images now generally available
articles.summary: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9 and RHEL 10 images for GitHub-hosted larger runners are now generally available. Originally introduced in public preview in June 2026 in partnership with Red Hat, these images are now fully supported for production workflows in GitHub Actions.

articles.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human.

articles.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
articles.summary: This paper presents an AI-driven framework, CodeReAct agent, designed to enhance industrial equipment maintenance through natural language (NL) interactions. The framework employs an advanced AI agentic approach to interpret human instructions, providing knowledge extraction, asset status summarization, and work order recommendations.

articles.title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
articles.summary: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS). For Market Split, our randomized algorithm searches across multiple lattice bases, dividing computation between enumeration and continued basis reduction.

articles.title: Check if that bargain SD card or USB drive is fake on Ubuntu
articles.summary: Check if a bargain SD card or USB drive has fake capacity on Ubuntu using F3 (Fight Flash Fraud), an open-source Linux alternative to h2testw.

articles.title: LibreOffice launch a TikTok account to reach a younger audience
articles.summary: TikTok addicts can now doomscroll videos about LibreOffice, which now has an official account on the platform. The Document Foundation’s Mike Saunders – a name familiar to former readers of the now-defunct magazine Linux Format – says the suite wants to “explore new places and ways” of reaching a younger audience.

articles.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released With More Performance Improvements
articles.summary: After running weeks behind schedule due to PostgreSQL developers being overwhelmed by AI/LLM-led bug reports and security issues, PostgreSQL 19.0 managed to finally ship today.

articles.title: PHP 8.6 Released With Partial Function Application, Other New Features
articles.summary: Following today's PHP 8.2.36, PHP 8.3.37, PHP 8.4.28, and PHP 8.5.13 security releases to address multiple security issues, PHP 8.6.0 made its official debut today.
